rows.headline: Calculating maturity value of monthly Sukanya Samriddhi investments
rows.hook: Projecting returns for Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
rows.summary: The Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) is a government-backed small savings scheme designed for the girl child with a 21-year maturity period. Investors contributing Rs 5,000 monthly can estimate their total corpus based on the prevailing interest rate, which is reviewed quarterly by the government. The scheme offers tax benefits under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act. Retail investors use these projections to plan long-term educational or marriage expenses for their children.

rows.why_it_matters: Helps parents estimate long-term savings for a daughter's future needs.

If Sagility B.V. is confirmed as the seller, its shareholding will drop below the 50 percent threshold, having stood at 50.95 percent at the end of the September quarter. This significant insider sell-off increases market supply and dilutes majority control. Indian retail shareholders face near-term price volatility and potential overhang from the reduced promoter backing.
rows.whats_next: Exchange disclosures confirming the block deal and seller identity
rows.why_it_matters: Promoter stake dilution brings near-term stock pressure for retail holders
rows.winners_losers: Institutional buyers gain / retail holders hurt

rows.headline: PM Modi to release ₹19,000 crore under PM-KISAN and inaugurate Bharat Parv
rows.hook: Massive direct cash transfer to farmers
rows.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will disburse the 19th installment of ₹19,000 crore under the PM-KISAN scheme to benefit millions of farmers. He will also inaugurate Bharat Parv in Kevadia, Gujarat. The PM-KISAN scheme provides direct income support of ₹6,000 per year to eligible farmer families across India in three installments. For retail investors, this capital infusion boosts rural liquidity, which typically supports demand for FMCG, fertilizer, and tractor stocks.
rows.whats_next: Disbursement event on release date
rows.why_it_matters: Rural liquidity boost supports consumer goods and agri-input demand
rows.winners_losers: Rural consumer goods firms gain / no clear losers

rows.headline: SEBI announces margin waiver on subsequent buy and sell transactions after early pay-in in cash segment
rows.hook: No extra margins for intraday trading after EPI
rows.summary: SEBI has granted a margin waiver for subsequent buy and sell transactions in the cash segment when an early pay-in (EPI) of securities has been made. This adjustment affects trading mechanics for market participants utilizing early pay-in facilities. Indian retail investors executing frequent intraday or delivery trades with early pay-in will see modified margin requirements. The move aims to streamline trading processes and optimize capital efficiency for cash segment participants.
rows.whats_next: Exchange circulars detailing operational implementation
rows.why_it_matters: Free up working capital for cash segment trades
rows.winners_losers: Active traders gain / brokers unaffected

rows.headline: SEBI orders attachment of Karan Subhashchandra Ravde's accounts
rows.hook: SEBI targets assets in India Infraspace case
rows.summary: SEBI has issued a recovery notice for the attachment of bank and post office accounts belonging to Karan Subhashchandra Ravde. This action is linked to Recovery Certificate No. 7137 of 2023 regarding the matter of India Infraspace Limited. The regulator is pursuing these assets to recover outstanding dues. This enforcement action highlights SEBI's ongoing efforts to penalize individuals involved in market violations.
rows.why_it_matters: Regulatory enforcement against individuals in specific company fraud cases.

rows.headline: Indian markets extend their previous session rally driven by IT stocks and Trent earnings
rows.hook: IT buying and Trent earnings drive continuation
rows.summary: Indian equity markets extended their previous session's gains, supported by buying interest in IT sector stocks. Strong earnings-driven demand in Trent also contributed to the upward momentum during the session. The broader market participation reflects ongoing investor appetite for select large-cap and earnings-backed equities. rows.headline: Coal India reports 53% profit growth and announces dividend
rows.hook: Coal India profit surges 53% annually
rows.summary: Coal India reported a net profit of Rs 6,275 crore for the September quarter, marking a 53% increase compared to the same period last year. The company's board has also declared an interim dividend of Rs 15.75 per share for the current financial year. This performance reflects robust operational efficiency despite seasonal challenges in the mining sector. Retail investors holding the stock will benefit from the dividend payout, with the record date set for November 5, 2024.
rows.whats_next: Dividend record date is November 5, 2024
rows.why_it_matters: Shareholders receive a cash payout of Rs 15.75 per share.
rows.winners_losers: Coal India shareholders gain
